I've been growing cotton on this plot for ten years now. It's only 1.5 mu — small, but it's mine, and I know every corner of it. Some of my family members have gone to work in the city or nearby factories, so I can't always count on them during busy periods. But for 1.5 mu of cotton, I can manage most of the work myself, and they help during the picking rush in September.

I'll stick with cotton again this year. I know the local buyers, I know the market, and I know my land. Switching crops on a whim doesn't make sense to me. Cotton fits our well irrigation — I can pump when the plant needs it, especially during the flowering and boll-setting stage in July and August when rain is unreliable.

For seeds, I'll buy hybrid Bt cotton again — the same type I've been using for the past several years. It cuts down on some of the bollworm spraying, and the yields have been decent. The seed cost is higher but worth it.

On fertilizer: I'll put down a base application of phosphorus and potassium before plowing, then topdress nitrogen in stages — at seedling stage, at budding, and then a heavier dose at flowering. That's how my neighbors do it and it's worked for me too. Around 15 kg of nitrogen total per mu feels right based on what I've seen over the years.

I'll irrigate about 5 times — once before planting to wet the soil deep, then follow the plant's needs through summer. I won't over-irrigate; pumping from the well costs money.

For pesticides, even with Bt cotton I spray for aphids early on and for spider mites in the heat. I figure 7 applications across the season, maybe fewer if we get a dry summer that keeps some pests down.

I'll plough the field before planting. The soil here compacts and I want good root development.

I expect around 250 kg of seed cotton per mu. Last year was close to that. If the weather cooperates, maybe a bit more.
